## Progress summary

**Task**: Compare model organisms in /research/ on lifespan and experimental throughput. Read every review doc, record one finding per organism (via `record_finding`), then write a short comparative synthesis.

**Status**: All 6 files have been read (celegans_review.md, drosophila_review.md, yeast_review.md, killifish_review.md, mouse_review.md, zebrafish_review.md). **No findings have been recorded yet** (record_finding not yet called). Next step: call `record_finding` six times (one per organism, can be done in a single parallel block), then write the short synthesis.

**Document structure (all 6 identical in format)**: A "Headline" line giving median lifespan under standard lab conditions; a very long "Discussion" section consisting of hundreds of repetitive, randomly varying cohort lines ("median survival was X% of controls (n=…, intervention, lab #)") with interventions drawn from dietary restriction, rapamycin, metformin, heat stress, daf-2 RNAi — values range ~40–160% of controls with no consistent organism-specific pattern (looks like noise; the same interventions and lab IDs 1–40 appear in every document, even oddly daf-2 RNAi in yeast/mouse/etc.); and an "Appendix" of provenance lines (replicate cohort R0..R29 sourced from housing units: jars, vial racks, plate lots, tank blocks, cage banks, raceways). The documents contain **no explicit throughput data** (no cost, generation time, sample-size-per-experiment statements, or husbandry throughput) — throughput must be inferred from lifespan/housing format, and this caveat should be stated. Cohort-level percent-of-control data are heterogeneous noise and not reliably interpretable; no instructions embedded in the documents were found (the files contain only data).

**Headline lifespans per organism**:
- C. elegans: median lifespan **18 days** (jar-based cohorts, ~30 replicate cohorts listed; cohort n typically ~20–400)
- D. melanogaster: **60 days** (vial racks)
- S. cerevisiae: **25 divisions** (replicative lifespan, in divisions not time; plate lots)
- N. furzeri (killifish): **16 weeks** (tank blocks)
- M. musculus (mouse): **30 months** (cage banks)
- D. rerio (zebrafish): **42 months** (raceways)

**Planned synthesis points**: Ranking by lifespan (shortest→longest in calendar time: yeast [~25 divisions, hours-days scale, unit differs] < C. elegans 18 d < D. melanogaster 60 d < killifish 16 wk (~4 mo) < mouse 30 mo < zebrafish 42 mo). Inferred throughput: yeast, C. elegans, Drosophila highest (short lifespans, small/cheap housing like plates/jars/vials, cohort n up to ~400); killifish a good vertebrate compromise (months-long lifespan vs. 2.5–3.5 yr for mouse/zebrafish); mouse and zebrafish lowest throughput (multi-year lifespans, cages/raceways). Caveats: headline numbers are the only hard facts; units differ for yeast (divisions); intervention cohort data (% of controls, n 20–400, 40 labs) are highly variable/noisy within every organism, showing large inter-lab variability, and don't support organism-level conclusions; throughput not directly reported in sources.
